local.heading: Fort Mill more than doubled in ten years, and new residents find businesses by searching.
paragraphs: Fort Mill grew up as a mill town. It was chartered in 1873 and named for a colonial-era fort and Webb's Mill, and town hall now sits in the former Springs Industries executive offices. Some buildings on Main Street date to the 1800s. The Census counted 10,811 people here in 2010 and 24,521 in 2020, and recent estimates put the town past 36,000. A family that moved in last spring doesn't know the local names yet, so they search.

The jobs came along with the houses. In 2014 LPL Financial and the Lash Group announced moves to Kingsley, the mixed-use development at the I-77 and Highway 160 interchange, and the Charlotte Business Journal put the two companies at 5,400 jobs combined. Domtar, Sunbelt Rentals and Shutterfly also have a presence in the area, and the Carolina Crown drum corps is headquartered here. That puts a daytime crowd of office workers on Highway 160 who eat, shop and book appointments close to work.

Fort Mill sits just south of the North Carolina line, with Charlotte to the north and Rock Hill to the south. Local businesses land in the same search results as a much bigger metro, so a local roofer or accountant can show up beside Charlotte firms with far larger budgets. Pages that say exactly where you work, backed by a Google profile that agrees, help Google match you to the searches happening near you.

The map confuses people too. Some homes and businesses in Indian Land, over in Lancaster County, use a Fort Mill mailing address even though they sit outside town limits. Tega Cay kids attend York County School District 4 with kids from town. Customers don't think in terms of those lines, so your site should use the place names people say out loud when they describe where they live.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Fort Mill businesses
paragraphs: We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, on the west side of metro Atlanta. Clients up here work with us mostly by video call and shared drafts. We learn your business and which parts of town and nearby communities you serve, then send a working version of the site that you can click through and mark up from your phone.

When it helps to be there in person, for photos or a planning session with your staff, we make the trip. Outside of that you get calls whenever you want them and a short monthly report showing calls, form fills and how your local search visibility is moving. You deal with the same two people the whole way.

faqs.q: How much does web design cost for a Fort Mill, SC business?
faqs.a: Most Fort Mill businesses start with our Local Marketing Package: $297 a month, month to month, no contract. It covers local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (the ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Mill business compete with Charlotte companies on Google?
faqs.a: For searches made in and around Fort Mill, often yes. Google leans on the searcher's location for local results. A site that clearly says you serve Fort Mill and the communities nearby, plus a full Google Business Profile with steady reviews, puts you in the running. Nobody can promise a ranking, and we won't.

faqs.q: My mailing address says Fort Mill but I'm in Indian Land. How should my site handle that?
faqs.a: Be accurate about both. Many Indian Land homes and businesses use a Fort Mill mailing address while sitting in Lancaster County. We set up your site and Google profile to match your real location and still mention the areas customers associate with you.

faqs.q: Should I have separate pages for Tega Cay and Baxter Village?
faqs.a: If you get work there, yes. A page written about that area, with the jobs you do there and reviews from those customers, usually does better than one generic page. If you don't serve a place, we leave it off the site.

faqs.q: Do I need to meet you in person?
faqs.a: No. We're based in Villa Rica, Georgia, and most projects run on video calls and drafts you review on your phone. When a visit would make the site better, like a photo day at your shop, we'll come up.

faqs.q: How fast can a new website go live?
faqs.a: Most sites launch within a few weeks of the first call. The schedule mostly depends on how quickly we get your photos, service list and notes on the draft. SEO setup runs alongside the build, so the site launches ready to be found.
